result.summary: Appends the canonical symlink-resolved path to the startup log entry for the active data directory whenever the resolved path differs from the nominal path. It calls std::filesystem::canonical with error checking so resolution failures are ignored silently.
result.problem: When a node's data directory or any parent directory is a symlink, debug.log records only the nominal path. Developers and node operators reviewing logs cannot verify the physical storage directory or underlying media used for that run.
evidence: PR description: 'I've been testing a potential performance PR across different data directories (for example, SSD versus HDD)... It would be nice if the debug.log file showed which data directory was used for that run.'
result.changed_since_previous: The resolved path is now appended in parentheses directly onto the existing 'Using data directory' log line instead of being printed on a separate line, and is only logged when it differs from the nominal path.
result.card: Appends the symlink-resolved canonical path to the startup data directory log line when it differs from the nominal path. This ensures debug.log captures the actual physical filesystem location used during execution, which the author notes helps when comparing benchmarks across different drives under wrapper scripts. Low priority logging improvement with no dependencies.

risk.why: Only changes a single startup informational log message using standard filesystem utilities.
